name: BACH_0238
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (100%)** · Confident · Careful review

Flagged tier 2: invasive is the top class and in the conformal set; confidence signals agree [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive 100%, InSitu <1% | Near-certain |
| Conformal set | {Invasive} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.998 / 86th percentile | No input flag |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes | Same top class |
| Similar cases | 5 of 5 Invasive | Unanimous |

## Tissue evidence
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 7, 9, 10) · ↑ invasive · Strongest concept association here [F2] · Validated
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 0, 7, 8) · ↑ invasive · Above-typical stromal invasion pattern [F3] · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (region 3) · ↑ invasive · Scarce tubules count toward invasive in concept model [F4] · Weak
- **Nuclear size** (regions 1, 2, 6) · context · 85 µm² mean, above 95% of reference images [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing top 3 regions drops invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion test shows no effect versus random (CI includes 0); not shown to reflect the classifier. Unreliable here: normal lobules (0/20), necrosis (3/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Calibration is imperfect: ECE 0.05 (CI 0.03–0.18) on 132 images, so 100% may be overstated.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 7, 9, 10:** Confirm marked nuclear pleomorphism.
2. **Regions 0, 7, 8:** Confirm tumor cells infiltrating stroma.
3. **Region 3:** Check whether benign glands explain the strongest tubule signal.
